Subject: EdgeWorks pilot — post-demo recap and pilot checklist

Thanks again for your time today, Luke + Sam — great discussion. Quick post-demo recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth to plan the pilot: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: validate latency & streaming behavior under production traffic patterns for the customer-facing recommendation API.
- Targets: p95 latency ~120ms (streaming responses acceptable), sustained throughput ~400 QPS during peak windows, concurrent active streams ~25, cold-starts less than 300ms for small prompts.
- Data: requests will contain short prompts (avg 120 tokens output), occasional long-context sessions (up to 2k tokens) during interactive flows.
- Security: pilot will run in Redwood Dedicated (VPC), EdgeWorks has strict audit log and retention needs (SOC2 evidence later).

Attachments I’m including: pilot SLO matrix (edgeworks_slo_matrix.xlsx) — fill in any missing numbers and return.

Proposed pilot scope & success criteria
- Pilot duration: 2 weeks of controlled traffic + 1 week of soak in prod-like environment.
- Success: 95th percentile latency <=120ms for streaming endpoints at target throughput; error rate <0.5%; no unplanned rollbacks.
- Pilot infra: reserved throughput pool that can be scaled between 200–600 QPS; we’ll validate two GPU configs (cost vs tail latency): H100-based and A100-based.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Luke: confirm final SLO numbers in attached spreadsheet and provide a sample 1-hour p95 from your current infra (if available) — due Wed 3/18.
2) Redwood (Soojin): produce conservative sizing options (A100 vs H100) + cost delta and short-run bench plan — internal by Thu 3/19.
3) Redwood (Karthik/Priyom): prepare a quick bench (2 small experiments) to validate streaming tail behavior for both GPU types — ready by Mon 3/22.
4) Contract/procurement: Sam to share any procurement constraints (PO timing, legal redlines) — ASAP.

If that looks right I’ll schedule a short kickoff for Wed 3/25 to align tooling, keys, and traffic generation.

Nice summary — added concrete recommendations below after an initial pass on likely performance tradeoffs. I attached our internal benchmark summary (rw_gpu-benchmarks_v3.pdf) with microbench results from last month that are a good proxy.

High-level recommendation (pilot):
- Recommended pilot config: 2x H100-80GB (reserved pool) with one A100-40GB hot-standby node for cost-sensitive fallback. Rationale: H100s show ~25–35% better p99 tail on streaming workloads in our microbench for 70B-class LLMs with KV-heavy workloads, which helps meet the 220ms p99 and 120ms p95 targets at target QPS.
- Capacity sizing: to hit sustained 400 QPS with headroom for 650 QPS bursts (short windows), reserve capacity equivalent to ~2 H100s (conservative) and enable burst autoscale to add up to 1–2 extra H100s or 3 A100s for short periods.
- Quantized fallback: int8 variant on A100 shows good p95 but degrades p99 by ~30ms in our bench; suggest using quantized A100 as fallback for cost-control during long tail events.

Bench plan (Priyom):
- Run 2x experiments per hardware profile (H100 x2, A100 x4)
- Traffic profile: 10-min warmup -> 60-min steady at 400 QPS with scheduled 5-min burst at 650 QPS at minute 30 -> 30-min cool-down. Collect p50/p95/p99, cpu/gpu util, kv-hit, latency distribution.
- Cold-starts: run 50 one-off short prompts staggered to measure cold p95.

Deliverables and timing:
- Priyom to run benches and hand raw metrics to me by Mon 3/22.
- I’ll draft the customer-facing sizing note and cost delta (H100 vs A100) by Tue 3/23.
- Soojin to coordinate pilot kickoff scheduling with the customer for Wed 3/25.

Next steps for Soojin: confirm these recommendations in a short note to Luke (include expected cost delta and pilot reservation footprint) and attach the bench summary when we have results.
